Appendix A Proof of lemmas for Theorem 1

A.1 Proof of Lemma 1

To simplify the notation, we write Z>i=(Zi+1,…,Zd)Z^{>i}=(Z^{i+1},\ldots,Z^{d}) for any 1≤i<d1\leq i<d and define Z<iZ^{<i}, Z≥iZ^{\geq i}, and Z≤iZ^{\leq i} analogously. In addition, we denote Z∖i≔(Z1,…,Zi−1,Zi+1,…,Zd)Z^{\smallsetminus i}\coloneqq(Z^{1},\dots,Z^{i-1},Z^{i+1},\ldots,Z^{d}) for any 1≤i≤d1\leq i\leq d. Using the chain rule, one can derive

𝖪𝖫(pZ1,…,Zd∥∏i=1dpZi)\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}\Big(p_{Z^{1},\ldots,Z^{d}}\,\big\|\,\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Z^{i}}\Big) =∫pZ1,…,Zd​(z1,…,zd)​log⁡∏i=1dpZi|Z>i​(zi∣z>i)∏i=1dpZi​(zi)​d​z1​…​d​zd\displaystyle=\int p_{Z^{1},\ldots,Z^{d}}(z^{1},\ldots,z^{d})\log\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Z^{i}\mid Z^{>i}}(z^{i}\mid z^{>i})}{\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Z^{i}}(z^{i})}\,\mathrm{d}z^{1}\ldots\,\mathrm{d}z^{d}
=∑i=1d−1∫pZ<i|Z≥i​(z<i∣z≥i)​d​z<i​∫pZ≥i​(z≥i)​log⁡pZi|Z>i​(zi∣z>i)pZi​(zi)​d​z≥i\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}\int p_{Z^{<i}\mid Z^{\geq i}}(z^{<i}\mid z^{\geq i})\,\mathrm{d}z^{<i}\int p_{Z^{\geq i}}(z^{\geq i})\log\frac{p_{Z^{i}\mid Z^{>i}}(z^{i}\mid z^{>i})}{p_{Z^{i}}(z^{i})}\,\mathrm{d}z^{\geq i}
=∑i=1d−1∫pZi,Z>i​(zi,z>i)​log⁡pZi|Z>i​(zi∣z>i)pZi​(zi)​d​zi​d​z>i\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}\int p_{Z^{i},Z^{>i}}(z^{i},z^{>i})\log\frac{p_{Z^{i}\mid Z^{>i}}(z^{i}\mid z^{>i})}{p_{Z^{i}}(z^{i})}\,\mathrm{d}z^{i}\,\mathrm{d}z^{>i}
=∑i=1d−1I⁡(Zi,Z>i),\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}I(Z^{i};Z^{>i}),

where the second step holds because pZd|Z>d​(zd∣z>d)=pZd​(zd)p_{Z^{d}\mid Z^{>d}}(z^{d}\mid z^{>d})=p_{Z^{d}}(z^{d}). This proves (21).

Turning to (22), let us fix an arbitrary j∈[d]j\in[d]. We shall apply the same identity as in (21) but choose an ordering of the random variables such that ZjZ^{j} placed last. Define

(Y1,…,Yd)≔(Z1,…,Zj−1,Zj+1,…,Zd,Zj).\displaystyle(Y^{1},\dots,Y^{d})\coloneqq(Z^{1},\dots,Z^{j-1},Z^{j+1},\ldots,Z^{d},Z^{j}).

Recognizing that the KL divergence is invariant to the ordering of the random variables, one has

𝖪𝖫(pZ1,…,Zd∥∏i=1dpZi)\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(p_{Z^{1},\ldots,Z^{d}}\,\big\|\,\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Z^{i}}) =𝖪𝖫(pY1,…,Yd∥∏i=1dpYi)=∑k=1d−1I(Yk;Y>k),\displaystyle=\mathsf{KL}(p_{Y^{1},\ldots,Y^{d}}\,\big\|\,\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Y^{i}})=\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}I(Y^{k};Y^{>k}),

where the last step applies (21) to the random sequence (Y1,…,Yd)(Y^{1},\dots,Y^{d}).

Note that for each 1≤k<d1\leq k<d, YkY^{k} is one of the random variables ZiZ^{i} with i≠ji\neq j and Y>k⊆Z∖iY^{>k}\subseteq Z^{\smallsetminus i}. Therefore, by the monotonicity of mutual information, one has

I⁡(Yk,Y>k)≤I⁡(Zi,Z∖i).I(Y^{k};Y^{>k})\leq I(Z^{i};Z^{\smallsetminus i}).

Summing over all i≠ji\neq j gives the desired bound in (22):

𝖪𝖫(pZ1,…,Zd∥∏i=1dpZi)≤∑i≠jI(Zi;Z∖i).\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(p_{Z^{1},\ldots,Z^{d}}\,\big\|\,\prod_{i=1}^{d}p_{Z^{i}})\leq\sum_{i\neq j}I(Z^{i};Z^{\smallsetminus i}).

This completes the proof of Lemma 1.

A.2 Proof of Lemma 2

Preparation: auxiliary sequence.

Before presenting the details, let us first make several preparations to address the statistical coupling issue mentioned in Section 4.

Consider the auxiliary sampling process where we want to unmask the token sequence except the ii-th token, i.e.,

X∖i=(X1,…,Xi−1,Xi+1,…,XL),X^{\smallsetminus i}=(X^{1},\dots,X^{i-1},X^{i+1},\dots,X^{L}),

and run the entropy sum-based sampling procedure (Algorithm 1) according to the order induced by the auxiliary permutation in (27):

Π∖i≔(Π1,…,ΠΠi−1−1,ΠΠi−1+1,…,ΠL).\displaystyle\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\coloneqq\big(\Pi_{1},\dots,\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}-1},\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}+1},\dots,\Pi_{L}\big).

For each t∈[L]t\in[L], let 𝒲t∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t} and 𝒟t∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t} denote the cumulative and incremental unmasking sets at iteration tt in this auxiliary sampling process, respectively. In addition, we denote their sizes by Wt∖i≔|𝒲t∖i|W^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}\coloneqq|\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}| and Dt∖i≔|𝒟t∖i|D^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}\coloneqq|\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}|.

Moreover, similar to the size envelopes (D¯t)t=1L(\overline{D}_{t})_{t=1}^{L} in (28), we define the size envelopes associated with the auxiliary process (D¯t∖i)t=1L(\overline{D}_{t}^{\smallsetminus i})_{t=1}^{L} recursively by D¯1∖i≔0\overline{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{1}\coloneqq 0, and for t≥2t\geq 2,

D¯t∖i≔{D¯t−1∖i,if​Dt−1∖i<D¯t−1∖i,2​Dt−1∖i,if​Dt−1∖i≥D¯t−1∖i.\displaystyle\overline{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}\coloneqq\begin{cases}\overline{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1},&\text{if}~~D^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1}<\overline{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1},\\ 2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1},&\text{if}~~D^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1}\geq\overline{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1}.\end{cases} (36)

Below we make several important observations about the auxiliary sampling process.

  1. 1.

    By construction, the auxiliary unmasking sets (𝒟t∖i)t≥1(\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t})_{t\geq 1} are produced by running Algorithm 1 using the auxiliary permutation Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}. Hence, for any iteration t≥1t\geq 1, the set 𝒟t∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t} is independent of the unmasking order Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} of token ii in the original process.

  2. 2.

    For any iteration t≥1t\geq 1, conditioned on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and (𝒲t−1∖i,X𝒲t−1∖i)(\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1}}), the unmasking set 𝒟t∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t} at iteration tt in the auxiliary process is deterministic.

  3. 3.

    Recall that tit_{i} denotes the iteration at which the token with index ii is unmasked in the original sampling process. Note that before this iteration, the original sampling process never uses the information contained in the ii-th token to determine unmasking sets and sample tokens. This implies that the unmasking sets and sampled tokens before iteration tit_{i} coincide between the original and auxiliary processes. In particular, 𝒲t∖i=𝒲t\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}=\mathcal{W}_{t} and 𝒟t∖i=𝒟t\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}=\mathcal{D}_{t} for all t<tit<t_{i} in both processes.

To proceed, we make explicit some statistical dependence.

  • •

    After conditioning on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i}, the only remaining randomness in the original sampling process that affects the iteration at which token ii is unmasked is the insertion position Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi. To highlight this, we write

    ti=ti​(Πi−1)\displaystyle t_{i}=t_{i}(\Pi^{-1}_{i})

    for the iteration at which token ii is unmasked when its insertion position is Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}.

  • •

    More generally, in the original sampling process, the unmasking set 𝒟ti\mathcal{D}_{t_{i}} containing token ii depends on Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} through both the iteration index and the order of token ii within that iteration. Hence, we write

    𝒟⁡(Πi−1)≔𝒟ti​(Πi−1)​(Πi−1)\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\Pi^{-1}_{i})\coloneqq\mathcal{D}_{t_{i}(\Pi^{-1}_{i})}(\Pi^{-1}_{i}) (37)

    to emphasize this dependence on the insertion position Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}.

  • •

    Now fix an iteration s∈[L]s\in[L] and condition on (𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)(\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1}}) and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}. Under this conditioning, the auxiliary unmasking set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}_{s}^{\smallsetminus i} and its size Ds∖iD^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} are deterministic. In the original sampling process, the set of insertion positions pp of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi that lead to ti​(p)=st_{i}(p)=s is precisely the unmasking set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} in the auxiliary process, i.e.,

    {p∈[L]:ti​(p)=s}=𝒟s∖i.\displaystyle\{p\in[L]:t_{i}(p)=s\}=\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}.

    To see this, note that each index except the last one in 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} has the property that the sum up to the following token is still below the threshold. Therefore, token ii can be inserted at any such position without changing the iteration at which it is unmasked. On the other hand, the last index in 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} is the one at which the cumulative sum including the following token exceeds the threshold. Therefore, for token ii to be unmasked at iteration ss, this is the last position at which it can be inserted.

  • •

    However, if token ii is inserted at position p∈𝒟s∖ip\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} so that it is unmasked at iteration ss in the original sampling process, the resulting unmasking set 𝒟s\mathcal{D}_{s} may still vary with pp, because a high entropy of token ii can lead to early termination of iteration ss. Accordingly, for positions p∈𝒟s∖ip\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}, we write

    Ds​(p)=|𝒟s​(p)|\displaystyle D_{s}(p)=|\mathcal{D}_{s}(p)|

    to denote the size of the original unmasking set at iteration ss when token ii is inserted at position pp in the permutation Π\Pi.

    More precisely, the set of all other unmasked tokens in the same iteration ss as token ii in the original process, is a subset of the ss-th unmasking set in the auxiliary process, i.e.,

    𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}=𝒟s​(p)∖{i}⊆𝒟s∖i,∀p∈𝒟s∖i.\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}=\mathcal{D}_{s}(p)\setminus\{i\}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s},\quad\forall\,p\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}. (38)

    This is because inserting token ii into position p∈𝒟s∖ip\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} in the permutation Π\Pi can only make iteration ss terminate earlier in the original process than in the auxiliary process since the entropy of token ii can be large.

  • •

    To organize these insertion positions, it is convenient to index them relative to the start of the ss-th auxiliary batch 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}. Recall Ws∖i≔|𝒲s∖i|W_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}\coloneqq|\mathcal{W}_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}| and Ds∖i≔|𝒟s∖i|D_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}\coloneqq|\mathcal{D}_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}|. For each absolute insertion position q∈[L]q\in[L], let

    r≔((q−1)modDs∖i)+1,\displaystyle r\coloneqq\big((q-1)\bmod D_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}\big)+1,

    be the relative position of qq within the set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}, and define

    Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)≔Ds​(r+Ws−1∖i).\displaystyle D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\coloneqq D_{s}(r+W_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}). (39)

    In other words, Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q) represents the size of the ss-th original unmasking set 𝒟s\mathcal{D}_{s} obtained when token ii is inserted at relative position rr within the ss-th auxiliary unmasking set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}. In particular, we introduce the module operation in (39) to handle the case when qq is larger than the auxiliary batch size Ds∖iD_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}.

  • •

    Finally, note that conditioned on ti​(p)=st_{i}(p)=s, the envelope D¯s\overline{D}_{s} is determined by the original process up to iteration s−1s-1, and therefore does not depend on the relative index qq of the insertion position pp within the ss-th auxiliary batch 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}.

Proof of Lemma 2.

Having the above preparations, we are ready to prove Lemma 2.

Our goal is to analyze the contribution of token ii to the expected KL sampling error in (26) by taking expectation with respect to the randomness of Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}, namely, the random insertion position Πi−1\Pi_{i}^{-1} of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi. Hence, for each p∈[L]p\in[L], define

F⁡(p)\displaystyle F(p) ≔𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i)≤η}.\displaystyle\coloneqq\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}})\leq\eta\big\}}. (40)

We can then express (26) as

𝔼X,Π[𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖{i}∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)≤η}]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X,\Pi}\Big[\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}_{t_{i}}\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\}}\Big]
=𝔼[F(Πi−1)]=𝔼X∖i,Π∖i[𝔼Πi−1[F(Πi−1)∣X∖i,Π∖i]].\displaystyle\qquad=\mathbb{E}\big[F(\Pi^{-1}_{i})\big]=\mathbb{E}_{X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}}\Big[\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[F(\Pi^{-1}_{i})\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big]\Big]. (41)

In what follows, we focus on the inner expectation with respect to Πi−1\Pi_{i}^{-1} in (41). As Πi−1\Pi_{i}^{-1} is uniformly distributed over [L][L] conditioned on X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}, we have

𝔼Πi−1[F(Πi−1)∣X∖i,Π∖i]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[F(\Pi^{-1}_{i})\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big]
=(i)1L∑p=1L𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\overset{(\mathrm{i})}{=}\frac{1}{L}\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}})\leq\eta\big\}}
=(ii)1L∑s=1L∑p=1L𝟙{ti(p)=s}𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i,X𝒲ti​(p)−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\overset{(\mathrm{ii})}{=}\frac{1}{L}\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}(p)=s\}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}(p)-1}})\leq\eta\big\}}
=(iii)1L∑s=1L∑p∈𝒟s∖i𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\overset{(\mathrm{iii})}{=}\frac{1}{L}\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
=(iv)1L∑s=1L∑q=1Ds∖i𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(q+Ws−1∖i)∖{i}∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\overset{(\mathrm{iv})}{=}\frac{1}{L}\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{D_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(q+W_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i})\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}} (42)

Here, (i) follows from the fact that Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} is uniformly distributed over [L][L] independent of X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and that conditioned on X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}, tit_{i} is determined given Πi−1=p\Pi^{-1}_{i}=p; (ii) rearranges the summation by grouping the insertion positions with the same iteration index tit_{i}; (iii) arises from the fact {p∈[L]:ti​(p)=s}=𝒟s∖i\{p\in[L]:t_{i}(p)=s\}=\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}; (iv) rewrites the position pp in terms of the relative position qq within the auxiliary unmasking set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}.

Next, let us swap the order of double summation in (42). The technical challenge is that the size of the second summation, or equivalently the size of the auxiliary unmasking set 𝒟s∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}, varies across different iterations ss. To ensure that the swapped summation is well-organized, we can leverage the dyadic size envelopes (D¯s)s=1L(\overline{D}_{s})_{s=1}^{L} to obtain an upper bound. This is established by the following lemma, whose proof is deferred to Appendix A.4.

Lemma 4.

Recall the definition of D¯s\overline{D}_{s} and Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q) in (28) and (39), respectively. The sum in (42) satisfies

∑s=1L∑q=1Ds∖i𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(q+Ws−1∖i)∖{i}∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{D_{s}^{\smallsetminus i}}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(q+W_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i})\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
≤∑s=1L∑k=sL∑q=12​Ds∖i∧Dk∖i𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(q+Wk−1∖i)∖{i}∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}.\displaystyle\quad\leq\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}\wedge D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(q+W_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i})\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}. (43)

Equipped with Lemma 4, we can continue the derivation. Recall (38) that

𝒟⁡(p)∖{i}⊆𝒟k∖i,∀p∈𝒟k∖i,\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(p)\setminus\{i\}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k},\quad\forall\,p\in\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k},

or equivalently, rewriting the absolute position pp in terms of the relative position qq within the auxiliary unmasking set 𝒟k∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}, we have

𝒟⁡(q+Wk−1∖i)∖{i}⊆𝒟k∖i,∀ 1≤q≤Dk∖i.\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(q+W_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i})\setminus\{i\}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k},\quad\forall\,1\leq q\leq D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}.

Using the monotonicity of mutual information, we can upper bound the right-hand side of (43) as

∑s=1L∑k=sL∑q=12​Ds∖i∧Dk∖i𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}𝙸(Xi;X𝒟⁡(q+Wk−1∖i)∖{i}∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}\wedge D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}(q+W_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i})\setminus\{i\}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
≤∑s=1L∑k=sL∑q=12​Ds∖i∧Dk∖i𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\leq\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}\wedge D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
≤∑s=1L∑q=12​Ds∖i𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad\leq\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
=2∑s=1L∑q=1Ds∖i𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad=2\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{q=1}^{D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}
=2∑s=1L∑p=1L𝟙{ti(p)=s}𝟙{Ds(p)≥D¯s}∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η},\displaystyle\quad=2\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}(p)=s\}\mathds{1}\{D_{s}(p)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}, (44)

where the penultimate step is due to the definition that Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q) is a function of qq modulo Ds∖iD^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}, and the last step is true because for q∈[Ds∖i]q\in[D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}], it corresponds to an insertion position pp such that ti​(p)=st_{i}(p)=s with Ds​(p)=Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D_{s}(p)=D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q).

Putting (43)–(44) together and substituting it into (42), we obtain that conditioned on X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},

𝔼Πi−1[F(Πi−1)∣X∖i,Π∖i]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[F(\Pi^{-1}_{i})\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big] ≤2L∑s=1L∑p=1L𝟙{ti(p)=s}𝟙{Ds(p)≥D¯s}\displaystyle\leq\frac{2}{L}\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}(p)=s\}\mathds{1}\{D_{s}(p)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}
⋅∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)≤η}.\displaystyle\qquad\cdot\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}\big(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big)\leq\eta\big\}}. (45)

To control the sum of the mutual information in the above display, the key insight is that the auxiliary unmasking sets satisfy 𝒲k∖i=𝒲k−1∖i∪𝒟k∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}=\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}\cup\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}, which allows us to leverage the chain rule of mutual information to control the sum. This is accomplished in the following lemma, whose proof can be found in Appendix A.5.

Lemma 5.

For any token index i∈[L]i\in[L] and iteration index s∈[L]s\in[L], one has

𝔼[∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}|𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\leq\eta\big\}}\,\big|\,\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\Bigg]
≤𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)∧η.\displaystyle\qquad\leq\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}})\wedge\eta. (46)

With the help of Lemma 5, let us compute the expectation over X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} on both sides of (45). For each s∈[L]s\in[L], the expectation of the ss-th term on the right-hand-side of (45) can be upper bounded as

𝔼[𝔼[∑p=1L𝟙{ti(p)=s}𝟙{Ds(p)≥D¯s}\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}(p)=s\}\mathds{1}\{D_{s}(p)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}
⋅∑k=sL𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}|𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i]]\displaystyle\quad\qquad\cdot\sum_{k=s}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}{\big\{\mathtt{H}\big(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{k-1}^{\smallsetminus i}}\big)\leq\eta\big\}}\,\Big|\,\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{W}_{s-1}^{\smallsetminus i}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\bigg]\Bigg]
≤(i)𝔼[∑p=1L𝟙{ti(p)=s}𝟙{Ds(p)≥D¯s}\displaystyle\quad\overset{(\mathrm{i})}{\leq}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{p=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}(p)=s\}\mathds{1}\{D_{s}(p)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\}

A.3 Proof of Lemma 3

We begin with the proof of (34). Recall from (17b) that for a fixed permutation Π=π\Pi=\pi, the data density can be expressed as

log⁡pX0​(x)=∑t=1τlog⁡p⁡(xdt∣xwt−1),\displaystyle\log p_{X_{0}}(x)=\sum_{t=1}^{\tau}\log p(x^{d_{t}}\mid x^{w_{t-1}}),

=𝔼X​[∑t=1T𝙷⁡(Xdt∣wt−1,Xwt−1,π)].\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{X}\Biggl[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathtt{H}(X^{d_{t}}\mid w_{t-1},X^{w_{t-1}},\pi)\Biggr].

We can then express the entropy of X0X_{0} as

H⁡(X0)\displaystyle H(X_{0}) =𝔼X∼pX0​[−log⁡pYT|Π=π​(X)−log⁡pX0​(X)pYT|Π=π​(X)]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim p_{X_{0}}}\biggl[-\log p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi=\pi}(X)-\log\frac{p_{X_{0}}(X)}{p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi=\pi}(X)}\biggr]
=𝔼X[−logpYT|Π=π(X)]−𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π=π)\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{X}\bigl[-\log p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi=\pi}(X)\bigr]-\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi=\pi})

A.4 Proof of Lemma 4

We prove Lemma 4 by showing that every term on the left-hand-side of (43) is covered by a term on the right-hand-side.

Fix an arbitrary 1≤k≤L1\leq k\leq L and 1≤q≤Dk∖i1\leq q\leq D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}. Recall the definitions of D¯s\overline{D}_{s} and Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q) in (28) and (39), respectively. Define

s=s⁡(k,q)≔max⁡{u≤k:D¯u≤q}.\displaystyle s=s(k,q)\coloneqq\max\big\{u\leq k\,:\,\overline{D}_{u}\leq q\big\}. (47)

This set is non-empty because D¯1=0\overline{D}_{1}=0, so ss is well-defined.

In what follows, let us show that the right-hand-side term with the index (s,k,q)(s,k,q) matches the term indexed by (k,q)(k,q) on the left-hand-side.

To begin with, let us verify that the indicator 𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\} is 11. We first claim that the relative size Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)D_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q) is at least qq, i.e.,

Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)≥q.\displaystyle D_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q)\geq q. (48)

To see this, recall that any position 1≤q≤Ds∖i1\leq q\leq D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} guarantees that token ii is unmasked at iteration ss. As the sampling process must first unmask the first q−1q-1 tokens in the batch and then unmask token ii, the unmasking set size must satisfy Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)=|𝒟s​(q)|≥qD_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q)=|\mathcal{D}_{s}(q)|\geq q. This establishes (48).

We can then combine (48) with the definition of ss in (47) to find

Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅​(q)≥q≥D¯s.\displaystyle D_{s}^{\mathsf{rel}}(q)\geq q\geq\overline{D}_{s}.

Thus the indicator 𝟙{Ds𝗋𝖾𝗅(q)≥D¯s}\mathds{1}\{D^{\mathsf{rel}}_{s}(q)\geq\overline{D}_{s}\} is 11.

As we choose q≤Dk∖iq\leq D_{k}^{\smallsetminus i}, it remains to prove that

q≤2​Ds∖i.\displaystyle q\leq 2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}.

If s=ks=k, then the above inequality holds trivially because q≤Dk∖i≤2​Ds∖iq\leq D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}\leq 2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}.

If s<ks<k, by the definition of ss in (47), we must have D¯s+1>q≥D¯s\overline{D}_{s+1}>q\geq\overline{D}_{s}. On the other hand, by the recursive definition of D¯s+1\overline{D}_{s+1} in (28), D¯s+1\overline{D}_{s+1} can only take a value in {D¯s,2​Ds}\{\overline{D}_{s},2D_{s}\}. This implies that D¯s+1=2​Ds\overline{D}_{s+1}=2D_{s}. Moreover, because q≤Dk∖iq\leq D_{k}^{\smallsetminus i} guarantees that token ii is unmasked at iteration kk with k>sk>s, we know that Ds=Ds∖iD_{s}=D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s} by by Observation A3. Therefore, this leads to

D¯s+1=2​Ds=2​Ds∖i>q.\overline{D}_{s+1}=2D_{s}=2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}>q.

Hence, in either case, we have

q≤2​Ds∖i∧Dk∖i.q\leq 2D^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}\wedge D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}.

This proves that each term indexed by (k,q)(k,q) on the left-hand-side corresponds to a term indexed by (s,k,q)(s,k,q) on the right-hand-side, and the proof of Lemma 4 is complete.

k0≔min⁡{s≤k≤L:𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η},k_{0}\coloneqq\min\Big\{s\leq k\leq L:\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}})\leq\eta\Big\},

Lemma 6.

For any random variables XX, Y1Y_{1}, Y2Y_{2}, and ZZ, the pointwise mutual information defined in (3) satisfies

𝙸(X;Y1,Y2∣Z)=𝙸(X;Y1∣Z)+𝔼Y1[𝙸(X;Y2∣Z,Y1)∣Z],\displaystyle\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z)=\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{1}\mid Z)+\mathbb{E}_{Y_{1}}\big[\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{2}\mid Z,Y_{1})\mid Z\big], (50)

=𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)\displaystyle\quad=\mathtt{I}\big(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big)
+𝔼X𝒟k∖i[𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k+1∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i,X𝒟k∖i)∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i]\displaystyle\quad\quad+\mathbb{E}_{X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}}\Big[\mathtt{I}\big(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k+1}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\big)\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\Big]

=(i)𝙸(Xi;X[L]∖𝒲k0−1∖i∣𝒲k0−1∖i,X𝒲k0−1∖i,Π∖i)\displaystyle\qquad\overset{(\mathrm{i})}{=}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{[L]\setminus\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})

≤(iii)​𝙷​(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)∧η.\displaystyle\qquad\overset{(\mathrm{iii})}{\leq}\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1}})\wedge\eta. (52)

where (i) holds since ⋃k=k0L𝒟k∖i=[L]∖𝒲k0−1∖i\bigcup_{k=k_{0}}^{L}\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}=[L]\setminus\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1}; (ii) is true because mutual information is always upper bounded by entropy, the entropy of XiX^{i} is independent of Π\Pi given 𝒲k0−1∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1} and X𝒲k0−1∖iX^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1}}, and the definition of k0k_{0} ensures that 𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲k0−1∖i,X𝒲k0−1∖i)≤η\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}-1}})\leq\eta; (iii) holds because 𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}}) is decreasing in kk and s≤k0s\leq k_{0}.

Finally, since 𝒲s∖i⊆𝒲k0∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s}\subseteq\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k_{0}}, we can take the expectation with respect to 𝒲s−1∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1} and X𝒲s−1∖iX^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1}} on both sides of (52) and use the tower property to conclude

𝔼[∑k=k0L𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)|𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i,Π∖i]≤𝙷(Xi∣𝒲s−1∖i,X𝒲s−1∖i)∧η,\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{k=k_{0}}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\,\big|\,\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\Bigg]\leq\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{s-1}})\wedge\eta, (53)

as claimed in (46). This completes the proof of Lemma 5.

A.6 Proof of Lemma 6

Fix an arbitrary zz with PZ​(z)>0P_{Z}(z)>0. By the definition of pointwise conditional mutual information in (3), we can express

I⁡(X;Y1,Y2∣Z=z)\displaystyle I(X;Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z=z) =𝔼X,Y1,Y2​[log⁡pX,Y1,Y2|Z​(X,Y1,Y2∣z)pX|Z​(X∣z)​pY1,Y2|Z​(Y1,Y2∣z)|Z=z].\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{X,Y_{1},Y_{2}}\biggl[\log\frac{p_{X,Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z}(X,Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid z)}{p_{X\mid Z}(X\mid z)\,p_{Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z}(Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid z)}\,\Big|\,Z=z\biggr].

Using the chain rule for conditional densities, we decompose the logarithm in the above display as

log⁡pX,Y1,Y2|Z​(X,Y1,Y2∣z)pX|Z​(X∣z)​pY1,Y2|Z​(Y1,Y2∣z)=log⁡pX,Y1|Z​(X,Y1∣z)pX|Z​(X∣z)​pY1|Z​(Y1∣z)+log⁡pY2|X,Y1,Z​(Y2∣X,Y1,z)pY2|Y1,Z​(Y2∣Y1,z).\displaystyle\log\frac{p_{X,Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z}(X,Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid z)}{p_{X\mid Z}(X\mid z)\,p_{Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z}(Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid z)}=\log\frac{p_{X,Y_{1}\mid Z}(X,Y_{1}\mid z)}{p_{X\mid Z}(X\mid z)\,p_{Y_{1}\mid Z}(Y_{1}\mid z)}+\log\frac{p_{Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},z)}{p_{Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},z)}.

Taking the expectation then gives

I⁡(X;Y1,Y2∣Z=z)\displaystyle I(X;Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z=z) =I⁡(X;Y1∣Z=z)+𝔼X,Y1,Y2​[log⁡pY2|X,Y1,Z​(Y2∣X,Y1,z)pY2|Y1,Z​(Y2∣Y1,z)|Z=z].\displaystyle=I(X;Y_{1}\mid Z=z)+\mathbb{E}_{X,Y_{1},Y_{2}}\biggl[\log\frac{p_{Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},z)}{p_{Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},z)}\,\Big|\,Z=z\biggr].

For the second term, applying the chain rule again yields

𝔼X,Y1,Y2​[log⁡pY2|X,Y1,Z​(Y2∣X,Y1,z)pY2|Y1,Z​(Y2∣Y1,z)|Z=z]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X,Y_{1},Y_{2}}\biggl[\log\frac{p_{Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid X,Y_{1},z)}{p_{Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},z)}\,\Big|\,Z=z\biggr]
=𝔼Y1[𝔼X,Y2[logpX,Y2|Y1,Z(X,Y2∣Y1,z)pX|Y1,Z​(X∣Y1,z)​pY2|Y1,Z​(Y2∣Y1,z)|Y1,Z=z]|Z=z]\displaystyle\qquad=\mathbb{E}_{Y_{1}}\Biggl[\mathbb{E}_{X,Y_{2}}\biggl[\log\frac{p_{X,Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z}(X,Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},z)}{p_{X\mid Y_{1},Z}(X\mid Y_{1},z)\,p_{Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z}(Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},z)}\,\Big|\,Y_{1},Z=z\biggr]\,\Big|\,Z=z\Biggr]
=𝔼Y1[I(X;Y2∣Z=z,Y1)∣Z=z].\displaystyle\qquad=\mathbb{E}_{Y_{1}}\bigl[I(X;Y_{2}\mid Z=z,Y_{1})\mid Z=z\bigr].

Hence, we obtain

I(X;Y1,Y2∣Z=z)=I(X;Y1∣Z=z)+𝔼Y1[I(X;Y2∣Y1,Z=z)].\displaystyle I(X;Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z=z)=I(X;Y_{1}\mid Z=z)+\mathbb{E}_{Y_{1}}\bigl[I(X;Y_{2}\mid Y_{1},Z=z)\bigr].

Using the definition of pointwise mutual information in (3), we conclude

𝙸(X;Y1,Y2∣Z)=𝙸(X;Y1∣Z)+𝔼Y1[𝙸(X;Y2∣Z,Y1)∣Z],\displaystyle\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{1},Y_{2}\mid Z)=\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{1}\mid Z)+\mathbb{E}_{Y_{1}}\bigl[\mathtt{I}(X;Y_{2}\mid Z,Y_{1})\mid Z\bigr],

as claimed in (50).

Taking the expectation with respect to ZZ on both sides of (50) then gives (51) immediately.

This completes the proof of Lemma 6.

Appendix B Proof of Theorem 2

B.1 Proof sketch of Theorem 2

The high-level proof strategy for Theorem 2 is similar to that for Theorem 1. Hence, we will mainly focus on the key differences in the analysis, and refer readers to Section 4.2 for the common technical details.

Step 1: Decompose KL error into sum of mutual information.

To begin with, since the sampling process of the maximum entropy-based strategy in Algorithm 2 also admits a Markovian structure (see (11)), the KL sampling error takes the same form as (20) in Section 4.2, i.e.,

𝔼Π[𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi}\big[\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi})\big] =𝔼Π,X∼pX0[∑t=1T𝖪𝖫(p𝒟t(⋅∣X𝒲t−1)∥∏i∈𝒟tpi(⋅∣X𝒲t−1))].\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\Pi,X\sim p_{X_{0}}}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathsf{KL}\Big(p^{\mathcal{D}_{t}}(\cdot\mid X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})\,\big\|\,\prod_{i\in\mathcal{D}_{t}}p^{i}(\cdot\mid X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})\Big)\Bigg].

It thus suffices to control the per-iteration KL error term in (19) for the maximum entropy-based strategy.

Recall that for the entropy sum-based strategy (Algorithm 1), we handle this term via the KL divergence bound in (22) from Lemma 1. Here, we instead apply the KL divergence identity (21) from the same lemma. Specifically, combining (21) with the representation of the unmasking set 𝒟t\mathcal{D}_{t} in (15):

𝒟t=𝒲t∖𝒲t−1={Π|𝒲t−1|+1,…,Π|𝒲t|},\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{t}=\mathcal{W}_{t}\setminus\mathcal{W}_{t-1}=\{\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t-1}|+1},\ldots,\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t}|}\},

we can express the KL error from iteration tt in (19) as

𝖪𝖫(pdt(⋅∣xwt−1)∥∏i∈dtpi(⋅∣xwt−1))\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}\Big(p^{d_{t}}(\cdot\mid x^{w_{t-1}})\,\big\|\,\prod_{i\in d_{t}}p^{i}(\cdot\mid x^{w_{t-1}})\Big)
=∑k=1|dt|−1I(Xπ|wt−1|+k;Xπ|wt−1|+k+1,…,Xπ|wt||(𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1)=(wt−1,xwt−1),Π=π).\displaystyle\qquad=\sum_{k=1}^{|d_{t}|-1}I\big(X^{\pi_{|w_{t-1}|+k}};X^{\pi_{|w_{t-1}|+k+1}},\ldots,X^{\pi_{|w_{t}|}}\,\big|\,(\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})=(w_{t-1},x^{w_{t-1}}),\Pi=\pi\big). (54)

That is, the contribution of iteration tt is given by a sum of mutual information terms, where the kk-th term measures the mutual information between the kk-th unmasked token and the tokens that are unmasked later within the same iteration. In particular, the last unmasked token in the iteration Xπ|wt|X^{\pi_{|w_{t}|}} does not contribute to the KL error.

Substituting (54) back into the expression of the KL sampling error (20) yields

𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π)\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi})
=𝔼[∑t=1T∑k=1|𝒟t|−1𝙸(XΠ|𝒲t−1|+k;XΠ|𝒲t−1|+k+1,…,XΠ|𝒲t|∣𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1,Π)]\displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{k=1}^{|\mathcal{D}_{t}|-1}\mathtt{I}(X^{\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t-1}|+k}};X^{\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t-1}|+k+1}},\dots,X^{\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t}|}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}},\Pi)\Bigg]
=𝔼[∑k=1L𝙸(XΠk;XΠk+1,…,XΠ|𝒲tΠk|∣𝒲tΠk−1,X𝒲tΠk−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(XΠk∣𝒲tΠk−1,X𝒲tΠk−1)<η}],\displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{\Pi_{k}};X^{\Pi_{k+1}},\dots,X^{\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t_{\Pi_{k}}}|}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{\Pi_{k}}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{\Pi_{k}}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{\Pi_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{\Pi_{k}}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{\Pi_{k}}-1}})<\eta\big\}\Bigg], (55)

where the second line reindexes by the absolute unmasking order k∈[L]k\in[L] instead of the relative order within each iteration. Here, we recall that tit_{i} denotes the iteration at which token ii is unmasked and thus tΠkt_{\Pi_{k}} stands for the iteration at which the kk-th unmasked token Πk\Pi_{k} is revealed. The indicator function arises because only non iteration-ending tokens contribute to the KL error and they satisfy the low-entropy condition by the maximum entropy-based stopping rule.

We next regroup the sum by token index i∈[L]i\in[L] instead of unmasking order k∈[L]k\in[L]. To this end, let ℒi\mathcal{L}^{i} be the index set of the tokens that are unmasked in the same iteration as token ii but are revealed after it, namely,

ℒi≔{ΠΠi−1+1,ΠΠi−1+2,…,Π|𝒲ti|}.\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{i}\coloneqq\big\{\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}+1},\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}+2},\dots,\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}}|}\big\}. (56)

Note that ℒi\mathcal{L}^{i} is a deterministic function of the permutation Π\Pi and the previous iterate (𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)(\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}}). Rewriting the sum in (55) accordingly yields

𝔼Π[𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi}\big[\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi})\big] =∑i=1L𝔼[𝙸(Xi;Xℒi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)<η}].\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{L}\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{L}^{i}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)<\eta\big\}\Big]. (57)

In a nutshell, this demonstrates that the expected KL sampling error can be decomposed into a sum of mutual information terms over token index i∈[L]i\in[L], where each term measures the correlation between token ii and the tokens that are unmasked later within the same iteration, conditioned on the tokens revealed in prior iterations and the permutation.

We note that in contrast to the analogous expression (25) for the entropy sum-based scheme, the mutual information term here involves only the tokens unmasked after token ii within the iteration, i.e., XℒiX^{\mathcal{L}^{i}}, rather than all other tokens in the same batch, i.e., X𝒟t1∖{i}X^{\mathcal{D}_{t_{1}}\smallsetminus\{i\}}.

Step 2: Bound KL error by entropy-based stopping rule.

Equipped with the KL error decomposition in (57), it suffices to fix a token index i∈[L]i\in[L] and focus on the ii-th term:

𝔼Π,X[𝙸(Xi;Xℒi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)<η}].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi,X}\Big[\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{L}^{i}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)<\eta\big\}\Big]. (58)

This is established in the following lemma; with proof deferred to Appendix B.2.

Lemma 7.

For any token index i∈[L]i\in[L], we have

𝔼X,Π∖i,Πi−1[𝙸(Xi;Xℒi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)<η}]≤SmaxLη.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X,\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\Big[\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{L}^{i}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}})<\eta\big\}\Big]\leq\frac{S_{\max}}{L}\eta. (59)

With Lemma 7 in hand, plugging (59) into (58) and summing over all token indices i∈[L]i\in[L], we find that the expected KL sampling error in (57) can be bounded as

𝔼Π[𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π)]≤Smaxη.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi}\big[\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi})\big]\leq S_{\max}\eta.

Setting the parameters as

Smax=ε​LH⁡(X0)andη=H⁡(X0)​SmaxL=ε​H​(X0)L\displaystyle S_{\max}=\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon L}{H(X_{0})}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\eta=\frac{H(X_{0})S_{\max}}{L}=\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon H(X_{0})}{L}}

yields the desired KL error bound 𝔼Π[𝖪𝖫(pX0∥pYT|Π)]≤ε\mathbb{E}_{\Pi}\big[\mathsf{KL}(p_{X_{0}}\parallel p_{Y_{T}\mid\Pi})\big]\leq\varepsilon.

Step 3: Control expected number of iterations.

As for the expected total number of iterations 𝔼⁡[T]\mathbb{E}[T], it is controlled by the following lemma; its proof is deferred to Appendix B.3.

Lemma 8.

The expected number of iterations 𝔼⁡[T]\mathbb{E}[T] is upper bounded as

𝔼⁡[T]≤2​LSmax+1.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[T]\leq\frac{2L}{S_{\max}}+1. (60)

In other words, the expected number of iterations is of the same order as if each iteration unmasks exactly SmaxS_{\max} tokens.

The claim in (12) then follows by plugging in the choice of SmaxS_{\max} into the above bound. We now complete the proof of Theorem 2.

B.2 Proof of Lemma 7

Our strategy is first to take the expectation over Πi−1\Pi_{i}^{-1}, the insertion position of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi. As in Lemma 2, the main technical challenge lies in the statistical dependence between ℒi\mathcal{L}^{i} (the set of tokens unmasked after token ii in iteration tt) and Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}, making it difficult to take the expectation over the randomness of Π\Pi in (58).

To this end, similar to the proof for Lemma 2 in Appendix A.2, we consider the auxiliary sampling process in which we unmask the entire token sequence except for the token with index ii. We work with X∖i=(X1,…,Xi−1,Xi+1,…,XL)X^{\smallsetminus i}=(X^{1},\dots,X^{i-1},X^{i+1},\dots,X^{L}) and run the maximum entropy-based sampling procedure (Algorithm 2) in the order induced by the permutation

Π∖i≔(Π1,…,ΠΠi−1−1,ΠΠi−1+1,…,ΠL).\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\coloneqq\big(\Pi_{1},\dots,\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}-1},\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}+1},\dots,\Pi_{L}\big).

This auxiliary sampling process produces a sequence of cumulative unmasking sets (𝒲t∖i)t=0L(\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t})_{t=0}^{L} and a sequence of unmasking sets (𝒟t∖i)t=1L(\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t})_{t=1}^{L}. Here, we slightly abuse notation and continue using 𝒲∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i} and 𝒟∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i} to denote the cumulative and incremental unmasking sets in the auxiliary process as in Appendix A.2, but now they are defined based on the maximum entropy-based sampling procedure instead of the entropy sum-based sampling procedure.

As before, we make several key observations.

  1. 1.

    For any iteration t≥1t\geq 1, conditioned on (𝒲t−1∖i,X𝒲t−1∖i)(\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t-1}}) and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}, the auxiliary sets (𝒟t∖i,𝒲t∖i)(\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t},\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t}) are fully determined. In addition, they are independent of the insertion position Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} for token ii.

  2. 2.

    By definition, 𝒟ti∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}} stands for the index set of tokens unmasked at the iteration where token ii is unmasked in the auxiliary sampling process. Because the auxiliary process never considers the token with index ii, the set 𝒟ti∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}} consists of either all low-entropy indices up to (and including) the first high-entropy index among indices not equal to ii, or low-entropy indices with size at most smaxs_{\max}. Consequently, the index set of tokens that are unmasked in the same iteration as token ii but after it in the original process must be a subset of the auxiliary unmasking set, i.e.,

    ℒi={ΠΠi−1+1,…,Π|𝒲ti|}⊆𝒟ti∖i.\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{i}=\big\{\Pi_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}+1},\dots,\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}}|}\big\}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}.
  3. 3.

    By construction, we have 𝒲k=𝒲k∖i\mathcal{W}_{k}=\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k} and 𝒟k=𝒟k∖i\mathcal{D}_{k}=\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k} for all 1≤k<ti1\leq k<t_{i}, and hence

    𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π∖i,Πi−1)\displaystyle\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{i}^{-1}) =𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i,Π∖i,Πi−1)\displaystyle=\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},\Pi^{-1}_{i})
    𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)\displaystyle\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}}) =𝙷⁡(Xi∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i).\displaystyle=\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}}).

In light of these observations, we can bound the target in (58) as

𝙸(Xi;Xℒi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)≤η}\displaystyle\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{L}^{i}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\}
≤𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1,X𝒲ti−1)≤η}.\displaystyle\quad\leq\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\}.
=𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i,Π∖i,Πi−1)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\quad=\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},\Pi^{-1}_{i})\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}\big(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\} (61)

where the second line arises from Observation B2 that ℒi⊆𝒟ti∖i\mathcal{L}^{i}\subseteq\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}} and the monotonicity of mutual information; the last line holds due to Observation B3.

Therefore, it suffices to control the right-hand side of (61). Towards this, we define the random variable

Gk\displaystyle G_{k} ≔𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i,Πi−1)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}\displaystyle\coloneqq\mathtt{I}\big(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},\Pi^{-1}_{i}\big)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}})\leq\eta\big\}
=𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η},\displaystyle=\mathtt{I}\big(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}})\leq\eta\big\}, (62)

for each k∈[L]k\in[L]. Here, the second line arises from Observation B1, namely, conditioned on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and (𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)(\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}}), 𝒟k∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k} is independent of Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}. 𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i)≤η}=Gti=∑k=1L𝟙{ti=k}Gk,\displaystyle\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\}=G_{t_{i}}=\sum_{k=1}^{L}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}=k\}G_{k}, (63)

To proceed, writing

𝔼[Gti]=𝔼X∖i,Π∖i[𝔼Πi−1[Gti∣X∖i,Π∖i]],\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[G_{t_{i}}\big]=\mathbb{E}_{X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}}\Big[\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[G_{t_{i}}\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big]\Big],

we focus on the inner expectation 𝔼Πi−1[Gti∣X∖i,Π∖i]\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[G_{t_{i}}\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big], where the expectation is taken over the randomness of Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i}, the insertion position of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi, conditioned on X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} and Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}.

By Observation B1 and the definition in (62), GkG_{k} is deterministic conditioned on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} for each k∈[L]k\in[L]. Therefore, the inner expectation can be computed as

𝔼Πi−1[Gti∣X∖i,Π∖i]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big[G_{t_{i}}\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big] =𝔼Πi−1[∑k=1LGk𝟙{ti=k}∣X∖i,Π∖i]=∑k=1LGkℙ{ti=k∣X∖i,Π∖i}.\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\Bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{L}G_{k}\mathds{1}\{t_{i}=k\}\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\Bigg]=\sum_{k=1}^{L}G_{k}\mathbb{P}\big\{t_{i}=k\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big\}. (64)

This suggests that we need to study the random iteration index tit_{i} at which token ii is unmasked in the original sampling process, which is determined by the insertion position Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} of token ii in the permutation Π\Pi. This is accomplished by the following lemma, whose proof is deferred to Appendix B.4.

Lemma 9.

Conditioned on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i}, the probability that token ii is unmasked at iteration kk in the original sampling process is upper bounded by

ℙΠi−1{ti=k∣X∖i,Π∖i}≤smaxL,∀k∈[L].\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{\Pi^{-1}_{i}}\big\{t_{i}=k\mid X^{\smallsetminus i},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i}\big\}\leq\frac{s_{\max}}{L},\quad\forall\,k\in[L].

≤smaxL​∑k=1LGk\displaystyle\leq\frac{s_{\max}}{L}\sum_{k=1}^{L}G_{k}
=smaxL∑k=1L𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η},\displaystyle=\frac{s_{\max}}{L}\sum_{k=1}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}})\leq\eta\big\},

where the last line follows from the definition of GkG_{k} in (62). Taking the expectation over Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i} on both sides, we obtain

𝔼⁡[Gti]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[G_{t_{i}}] ≤smaxL𝔼[∑k=1L𝙸(Xi;X𝒟k∖i∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i,Π∖i)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲k−1∖i,X𝒲k−1∖i)≤η}].\displaystyle\leq\frac{s_{\max}}{L}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{L}\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}},\Pi_{\smallsetminus i})\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}})\leq\eta\big\}\Bigg]. Plugging this into (65) and combining it with (63), we can bound the expectation of the right-hand side of (61) by

𝔼[𝙸(Xi;X𝒟ti∖i∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i,Π)𝟙{𝙷(Xi∣𝒲ti−1∖i,X𝒲ti−1∖i)≤η}]≤smaxLη.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[\mathtt{I}(X^{i};X^{\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}}}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}},\Pi)\mathds{1}\big\{\mathtt{H}(X^{i}\mid\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1},X^{\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t_{i}-1}})\leq\eta\big\}\big]\leq\frac{s_{\max}}{L}\eta.

B.3 Proof of Lemma 8

By the termination condition of the maximum entropy-based sampling procedure, we can split iterations into three types:

  • •

    cap iterations: end because Dt=|𝒟t|=smaxD_{t}=|\mathcal{D}_{t}|=s_{\max};

  • •

    high-entropy iterations: end because the stopping token has entropy exceeding η\eta;

  • •

    the final iteration, which contributes at most 1 to the total number of iterations TT.

Let T𝖼𝖺𝗉T_{\mathsf{cap}} and T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁T_{\mathsf{high}} denote the number of the first two types, respectively. We have T≤T𝖼𝖺𝗉+T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁+1T\leq T_{\mathsf{cap}}+T_{\mathsf{high}}+1.

For T𝖼𝖺𝗉T_{\mathsf{cap}}, since each cap iteration unmasks smaxs_{\max} tokens, we have

T𝖼𝖺𝗉≤L/smax.\displaystyle T_{\mathsf{cap}}\leq L/s_{\max}. (66)

Therefore, the remainder of the proof focuses on controlling 𝔼⁡[T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁]\mathbb{E}[T_{\mathsf{high}}].

Fix an arbitrary t∈[T]t\in[T]. Suppose that the tt-th iteration is a high-entropy iteration. Let it∈𝒟ti_{t}\in\mathcal{D}_{t} be the index of the last unmasked token at iteration tt, i.e., it=Π|𝒲t|i_{t}=\Pi_{|\mathcal{W}_{t}|}. By the stopping rule, we know that

η<𝙷⁡(Xit∣Π,𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1)≤𝙷⁡(X𝒟t∣Π,𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1),\displaystyle\eta<\mathtt{H}(X^{i_{t}}\mid\Pi,\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})\leq\mathtt{H}(X^{\mathcal{D}_{t}}\mid\Pi,\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}}),

where the last inequality follows from the monotonicity of entropy. This implies that

𝟙​{iteration ​t​ is high-entropy}≤1η​𝙷​(X𝒟t∣Π,𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1).\displaystyle\mathds{1}\{\text{iteration }t\text{ is high-entropy}\}\leq\frac{1}{\eta}\mathtt{H}(X^{\mathcal{D}_{t}}\mid\Pi,\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}}).

Summing over t∈[T]t\in[T] and taking expectation, we obtain

𝔼⁡[T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[T_{\mathsf{high}}] ≤1η​𝔼​[∑t=1T𝙷⁡(X𝒟t∣Π,𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1)].\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\eta}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathtt{H}(X^{\mathcal{D}_{t}}\mid\Pi,\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})\Bigg]. (67)

As shown in (34) from Lemma 3, we know that the sum on the right-hand side of the above display satisfies

𝔼⁡[∑t=1T𝙷⁡(X𝒟t∣Π,𝒲t−1,X𝒲t−1)]=H⁡(X0),\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathtt{H}(X^{\mathcal{D}_{t}}\mid\Pi,\mathcal{W}_{t-1},X^{\mathcal{W}_{t-1}})\Bigg]=H(X_{0}),

Consequently, we obtain

𝔼⁡[T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁]≤H⁡(X0)η=Lsmax,\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[T_{\mathsf{high}}]\leq\frac{H(X_{0})}{\eta}=\frac{L}{s_{\max}}, (68)

where the last step is due to our choice η=H⁡(X0)​smax/L\eta=H(X_{0})s_{\max}/L.

Combining (66) and (68), we conclude that

𝔼⁡[T]≤𝔼⁡[T𝖼𝖺𝗉]+𝔼⁡[T𝗁𝗂𝗀𝗁]+1≤2​Lsmax+1.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[T]\leq\mathbb{E}[T_{\mathsf{cap}}]+\mathbb{E}[T_{\mathsf{high}}]+1\leq\frac{2L}{s_{\max}}+1.

B.4 Proof of Lemma 9

Fix an arbitrary token index i∈[L]i\in[L] and condition on an arbitrary realization of Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i}. Recall the auxiliary sampling process defined by removing token ii. Conditioned on Π∖i\Pi_{\smallsetminus i} and X∖iX^{\smallsetminus i}, the auxiliary unmasking sets (𝒟t∖i,𝒲t∖i)t∈[L](\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t},\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{t})_{t\in[L]} are deterministic.

Because Π\Pi is uniformly random over all permutations of [L][L], after conditioning on the relative order of all indices except ii, the insertion position Πi−1\Pi^{-1}_{i} of token ii is uniformly random over [L][L]:

ℙ{Πi−1=r∣Π∖i,X∖i}=1L,r=1,…,L.\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\big\{\Pi^{-1}_{i}=r\mid\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},X^{\smallsetminus i}\big\}=\frac{1}{L},\quad r=1,\dots,L.

Now fix an arbitrary k∈[L]k\in[L] and consider the event {ti=k}\{t_{i}=k\}, i.e., token ii is unmasked at iteration kk in the original sampling process. By Observation A3, the original and auxiliary processes coincide before iteration kk. In particular, both processes have unmasked the same set of tokens 𝒲k−1∖i\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}. Therefore, token ii must appear after the first Wk−1∖i=|𝒲k−1∖i|W^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}=|\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}| tokens in the full permutation Π\Pi, implying that the insertion position of token ii satisfies Πi−1>Wk−1∖i\Pi^{-1}_{i}>W^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}.

Meanwhile, during iteration kk, before token ii is encountered, the original process sees exactly the same previously revealed tokens and the same sequence of candidate indices as the auxiliary process. Hence, before reaching token ii, it cannot proceed past the stopping point of iteration kk in the auxiliary process. In particular, if ii were inserted after the block 𝒟k∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}, then the original process would stop iteration kk before unmasking token ii. Thus, token ii must be inserted within the block of permutation positions corresponding to 𝒟k∖i\mathcal{D}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}, which means that the insertion position of token ii satisfies Πi−1≤Wk∖i=|𝒲k∖i|\Pi^{-1}_{i}\leq W^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}=|\mathcal{W}^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}|.

Combining the above two observations, we find

ℙ{ti=k∣Π∖i,X∖i}\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\bigl\{t_{i}=k\mid\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},X^{\smallsetminus i}\bigr\} ≤ℙ{Wk−1∖i<Πi−1≤Wk∖i∣Π∖i,X∖i}=Dk∖iL≤smaxL,\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{P}\bigl\{W^{\smallsetminus i}_{k-1}<\Pi^{-1}_{i}\leq W^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}\mid\Pi_{\smallsetminus i},X^{\smallsetminus i}\bigr\}=\frac{D^{\smallsetminus i}_{k}}{L}\leq\frac{s_{\max}}{L},

where the last step holds because by construction of the maximum entropy-based scheme, each iteration unmasks at most smaxs_{\max} tokens.

As the above bound holds for any k∈[L]k\in[L], we finish the proof of Lemma 9.
